clue.text: Keen to have dispute when time is limited

indicators.note: the dispute word limits, or hems in, the time letter, so one sits inside the other

blocks.note: to argue is to dispute
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to pick a quarrel whenever there is little time to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Argute is an old word for shrewd or sharp-witted, which is one sense of keen.

clue.text: Hedgehog in heather is so needly

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across heatHER IS SO Needly

explanation.surface: A spiky hedgehog is lurking in heather that is so prickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the French word for hedgehog, borrowed into English, mostly as a term in heraldry and fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: Herisson is the French-derived name for the animal, used in English mainly for a spiked defensive beam or in heraldry.

clue.text: Revolutionary made a beastly sound, responded loudly as before

blocks.note: a revolutionary is a rebel
cattle low, so lowed is a beast's sound

explanation.surface: An agitator mooed like a cow, then answered back in a booming voice just as before.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebellow is to bellow again or echo back, so loudly answering once more fits.

clue.text: Awfully idle in old age

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out in a wrong order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone spends their retirement doing nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Eild is a Scots and archaic word meaning old age or advanced years.

clue.text: Most perverse folk with a drink problem entering empty club

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, keeping only the two end letters
entering means going inside, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: a club is a bat; empty leaves its outer letters
alkies is slang for alcoholics

explanation.surface: The most awkward customers are drunks barging into a deserted nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Balky means stubborn and contrary, so its superlative names the most perverse.

clue.text: Certain snakes to glide away with tail disappearing

indicators.note: a disappearing tail means the last letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: time is said to elapse, or glide away

explanation.surface: Snakes slither off out of sight, the end of their tails vanishing last.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaps is a genus of venomous snakes related to the cobras, so the name covers certain snakes.

clue.text: Fish bordering church window

indicators.note: to border something is to lie around its edges, so the fish word wraps the church letters

blocks.note: lant is a dictionary name for the sand eel
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A stained-glass fish is pictured round the edge of a church window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church window' reads as one phrase, but church supplies letters and window alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancet is a tall narrow pointed window, typical of Early English Gothic architecture.

clue.text: Experts offering big lies

blocks.note: first meaning: people who are first-rate at something
second meaning: whoppers, outrageous untruths

explanation.surface: Specialists are found to be spinning enormous falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a oner is both an expert, a one-off ace, and a single great whopper of a lie.

clue.text: Cross once about attack interrupting merrymaking

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cross word surrounds another
interrupting means breaking into the middle of something

blocks.note: wry once meant cross or contrary
to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: Someone who was once angry launches an assault that breaks up a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailry is festive drinking and revelry, from the old toast wassail.

clue.text: Old-fashioned pattern of French art seen in physics unit

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the dyne is the CGS unit of force
in French, thou art is tu es

explanation.surface: A dated design taken from French art turns up in a physics measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: Art is not painting here but the old second-person form of be, whose French equivalent is es.
explanation.definitionFit: Desyne is a Spenserian spelling of design, an archaic word for a plan or pattern.

clue.text: Like nerves maybe in second test when there's a run out

indicators.note: run out says the cricket abbreviation for run is taken away

blocks.note: a second trial, or test
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run; this is removed

explanation.surface: A cricketer's nerves fray in the second Test match when a batsman is run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Retial means forming a network, like a rete, and nerves can form such a mesh, hence the maybe.

clue.text: Good person thus allied is to become dull

indicators.note: thus says the good person placed before the defined word makes the next phrase, so taking it off leaves the answer

blocks.note: to stagnate is to become stale and dull
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person; it is the part removed

explanation.surface: A virtuous person allied to others is doomed to grow tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards from the usual: saint plus the answer equals the phrase at the end, so remove the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnate means related through the male line, and more loosely akin or allied.

clue.text: Screen in dining room

blocks.note: first meaning: a grating or grille used as a screen
second meaning: a ... room, a restaurant serving ... food

explanation.surface: A partition stands in a restaurant's dining area.
explanation.definitionFit: Grill is a variant of grille, a lattice screen, and short for grill room, a place to eat.

clue.text: A refusal by English girl creates a sort of sensation

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: taken as written
no is a refusal
E is the abbreviation for English
sis is short for sister, a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from England saying no causes quite a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Anoesis is a philosophical term for mental experience that is pure feeling without understanding.

clue.text: Help for people not in workhouse fantastic, willingly given

definitions.text: Help for people not in workhouse

blocks.note: outré means bizarre or fantastic
lief is an old word for gladly or willingly

explanation.surface: Charity for those outside the workhouse is wonderful when freely handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: A workhouse was a Victorian British institution where the poor lived and worked in return for relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrelief was poor-law assistance paid to paupers who lived at home rather than inside a workhouse.

clue.text: Ladies perhaps in vehicle, attractive but denied kiss

indicators.note: being denied something means going without it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
sexy means attractive
X is the kiss at the end of a letter; it is removed

explanation.surface: Some women in a car, glamorous but refused a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladies is the British term for a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Carsey is British slang for a lavatory, and the Ladies is one example of such a room.

clue.text: Decay around is producing woe

indicators.note: turned around means read from the other end

blocks.note: rust is decay of metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rot all about the place is causing misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsuris is Yiddish-derived slang for trouble or misery, so it matches woe.

clue.text: This came to be artistic movement

indicators.note: came to be suggests becoming something different, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the first letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: This is how a new movement in art came into being.
explanation.walkthrough: Came serves twice: its letters are fodder, and with to be it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tachisme was a French abstract painting style of the 1940s and 50s using blots and splashes of colour.

clue.text: Irritate expert — last character to savour old-fashioned strife

indicators.note: last character points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
the final letter of savour
bate is an obsolete word for strife or contention

explanation.surface: An expert irritates others, being the final person to enjoy outdated quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbate means to embitter or exasperate, a close synonym of irritate.

clue.text: A setter somehow has to be exact

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler somehow needs to be precise.
explanation.walkthrough: Exact is the verb, to demand payment, not the adjective meaning precise.
explanation.definitionFit: To estreat is a legal term for extracting a forfeited fine or bail, which is to exact payment.

clue.text: Parasites attaching to a woman

indicators.note: attaching to means joining on, so the pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: taken as written
lice are parasites

explanation.surface: Parasitic insects latch on to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a girl's name, and crosswords use any forename as a woman or man.

clue.text: Principles of Henry VIII's opponent

blocks.note: first meaning: the customs and moral codes of a society
second meaning: belonging to Thomas More, who opposed Henry VIII and was executed

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More refused to accept Henry VIII as head of the English church; the possessive of his name gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the moral conventions of a group, its guiding principles, and More's means belonging to More.

clue.text: Agents providing publicity for clothes-hire firm?

indicators.note: for, read as on behalf of, puts the firm name next to the publicity word

blocks.note: Moss Bros is a British firm that hires out formal suits
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Spies are doing the advertising for a dress-hire company.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss Bros is a British chain that hires out morning suits and dinner jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Mossad is Israel's national intelligence agency, whose operatives are secret agents.

clue.text: Flighty type — minor drudge working on the paper?

blocks.note: a hack is a drudging journalist
-let is a suffix meaning small

explanation.surface: An unreliable sort is a junior newspaper dogsbody.
explanation.walkthrough: Flighty suggests fickle, but here it means able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacklet is a dialect name for the kittiwake or shearwater, a seabird, so a type that takes flight.

clue.text: Listens to end of commentary that's funereal

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: hears means listens to
the final letter of commentary

explanation.surface: Someone tunes into the close of a commentary that sounds like a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsy means like a hearse, hence gloomy and mournful.

clue.text: Ruddy bully endlessly grabbing one

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter goes
grabbing means seizing hold of, so the shortened word wraps round another

blocks.note: a tyrant is a bully
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A blasted bully, never stopping, picks on one.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddy looks like a mild British oath, as in ruddy nuisance, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrian purple, the ancient dye of Tyre, is a crimson colour, so Tyrian can mean ruddy or red.

clue.text: Depression's evident in short Oxford term

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Hilary is the Oxford University term after Christmas

explanation.surface: Students get gloomy in a brief spell of the Oxford university year.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression here is the botanical or anatomical sense, a small hollow, not low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilar describes a hilum, a dent or scar where vessels enter an organ or seed, so where such a hollow appears.

clue.text: Good prince in wheeled vehicle

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
Prince Harry of the British royal family

explanation.surface: A well-behaved royal rides in a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gharry is a horse-drawn cab used in India and Egypt, a kind of wheeled vehicle.

clue.text: Brightness of learner in extraordinary game

in places one letter inside the other piece

blocks.note: L is the learner driver's plate
the letters to rearrange

explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a flash or glow of light, so brightness.

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of Sarah
in means at home
taken as written

clue.text: Pollution as before certain to include greasy liquid

clue.text: Tribes are hiding with monkey around

clue.text: Explains part of building to daughter and son

clue.text: Flowery bits presented with the last word followed by cheers

clue.text: Beam shown by fellows when expert's brought round financial allocation

fellows are men
